evidence: instruction.md (116 words, 3 short paragraphs) reads as a person describing their own habit: instruction.md:1 "I'd like a small local playground ... I often paste a long one-line experiment, format it, make changes in several places, and then run it beside the source." and instruction.md:5 "I should be able to open it, edit code, run it and inspect the result without signing in." Sentence length varies, there is a contraction, no bullets, no numbered lists, no headings. A grep over instruction.md and all six notes for marketing gloss and LLM tells (seamless, robust, delve, leverage, comprehensive, intuitive, ensure, utilize, streamline, crucial, furthermore, moreover, additionally, em/en dashes) returned zero hits, and there are no bulleted or numbered lists in any of the seven files, so the skill's defects 'marketing gloss' and 'perfectly parallel bullets' are absent. First person carries into the notes, so the voice does not flip to an anonymous spec: overview.md:3 "while I work"; behaviour.md:11 "That refresh must not touch what I am doing ... say so and keep my draft; do not load the newer revision over my work."; ui.md:3 "as long as the source I see is drawn by your own surface"; ui.md:9 "whichever you prefer"; policy.md:3 "A parser or formatter library is fine". Cadence is mixed, with short sentences such as behaviour.md:5 "A restored picture may be static." and behaviour.md:13 "History inspection is read-only." next to long ones. Residual observation (not a defect under the workbook wording, which accepts casual/terse but does not require it): the register tightens between instruction.md and the notes. The six notes (1,721 words) contain zero contractions (grep finds only possessives; e.g. behaviour.md:11 "what I am doing", ui.md:3 "Do not use a textarea"), about 15 uses of 'must', and no sentence fragments, whereas quality-checks.md:14 says to verify "contractions, the occasional terse fragment in the notes". integration.md:3 also switches to "We start it with node /app/server.js" while the other notes say "I"; that mirrors the template's impersonal integration note and is a plausible deploy-side plural. None of this reads as robotic or LLM-generated; it reads as a careful person writing precise notes. No runtime measurement applies to this row.
suggested_fix: Optional, wording only and without changing any requirement: let a few contractions into the notes where the owner already speaks in first person (e.g. behaviour.md:11 "what I'm doing", "don't load the newer revision over my work"; ui.md:3 "Don't use a textarea...") so the notes match the register of instruction.md:1. Any such edit creates a new candidate and invalidates this clearance.
